newsitem.title: USA: Manufactured Home spices up offer for Chateau.
newsitem.headline: Manufactured Home spices up offer for Chateau.

text.p: Chicago investor Sam Zell, trying to edge out a Colorado rival in the courtship of Chateau Properties Inc., said Thursday he revised his $400 million bid for the real estate concern to provide a tax shelter for the majority of Chateau's current owners.

Zell, through his real estate investment trust, Manufactured Home Communities Inc., said the revised bid included a class of tax-deferred convertible preferred securities for Chateau's operating partners and an all-cash bid for its common stock.

The total cash value of the deal would not change from the $400 million already bid, but it could entice the partners to sell out by providing a shelter from what otherwise might be a sizeable -- and taxable -- capital gain.
Manufactured Home is locked in a battle for Chateau with ROC Communities Inc. of Colorado. All three concerns operate mobile home parks.

Chateau, based in Clinton Township, Mich., said it "will carefully review the proposal in due course," but in the meantime remained committed to its existing merger agreement with ROC, a combination that would create the largest company in the mobile home park industry.
The agreement between ROC and Chateau would give Chateau's holders 1.0316 share of the combined company for each share they now hold.

Manufactured Home's revised bid includes a class of securities valued at $26 each for each of the partners' ownership units and includes a long-term tax deferral and protection against a drop in the value of Manufactured Home, the company said in a news release.
It also includes $26 a share in cash for each of Chateau's shares of common stock, which is unchanged from its previous bid.
Manufactured Home also said it would drop its strategy of pursuing Chateau through the courts and terminate its hostile tender offer of $26 a share.
"We concluded that going through the courts most likely was not going to get us to our ultimate goal," said Cindy McHugh, a spokeswoman for Manufactured Home.
In the past Chateau has said it was not for sale, and if it were, $26 a share would not be enough to buy it.

"I think he (Zell) has recognised that the cost of being aggressive and hostile is pretty expensive, and I'm not sure the end result would have been too predictable," said Jim Sullivan, an analyst for Green Street Advisors. "Although (Manufactured Home) has a good case, you never know."

Another analyst, who spoke on condition he not be identified, said, "They (Chateau) should by all rights accept the offer. But I think they like the panache of being chairman, CEO or whatever of a New York Stock Exchange traded company, and they know Sam Zell would boot them out."
Chateau's shares closed at $24.625, up 25 cents a share. Manufactured Home closed at $19.50, down 12.5 cents, and ROC closed at $24.625, up 12.5 cents, all on the New York Stock Exchange.

The bidding war began in July when ROC and Chateau initially agreed to merge into one company, Chateau Communities, with Chateau stockholders receiving one share of the merged company per Chateau share.
Manufactured home followed with a bid of its own and launched a hostile tender offer.
Chateau subsequently urged its shareholders not to tender their shares and revised its agreement to sweeten the deal with ROC for its stockholders.
